A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places this state/province among its low-risk group: it has largely refrained from targeting transgender adults, and although it has enacted policies affecting trans youth, the map's author considers them unlikely to be extended to adults. That is the assessment's praise of restraint, not of protection — no extraordinary protective measures are recorded for this state/province.

The local scene has tracked the national chill: the historic 2026 Pride celebration in this state/province was cancelled, citing a political and financial environment that made hosting nearly impossible and attending potentially unsafe.
rewrites.blindTangential: The 2026 Pride cancellations are an LGBT+-visibility conflict rather than a trans-specific measure, but they track the same climate of official hostility that shapes enforcement posture.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: This state/province's anti-trans enacted law of the 2022-26 window is a ban on surgical care for transgender minors (2022); a 2023 governor's executive order added shield-style protections for lawful transgender health care in the state/province — youth-care questions are resident-facing, not visitor-facing.

A news outlet (3 Jun 2026): a Pride organisation in this state/province cancelled all 2026 events in January and effectively dissolved, citing a political and financial environment that made supporting queer events nearly impossible; it was grouped with two other cities as affected cities.

rewrites.blindSummary: Highest legal floor in the country: the first sanctuary law for transgender care in any state/province (signed 2022) and shield protections against out-of-state/province enforcement. But also the most recorded incidents of any state/province in 2025 (198), a "dramatic increase" in hate-crime reports, and 34 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (4.1 per 100k). Above the national score 0.36; law and street volume pull opposite ways.
rewrites.blindTangential: The incident counts cover anti-LGBTQ hostility broadly (drag events, pride disruptions as well as trans-targeted abuse), and the killing rate specifically tracks trans women — volume metrics mix adjacent categories.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: The law's shields (medical-record privacy, bars on out-of-state/province investigations, arrests and cooperation around gender-affirming care) principally protect residents, patients, providers and families moving here; a short-term visitor invokes them only as a signal of official posture.
rewrites.blindOutOfScope: General crime and road-safety conditions in this state/province are ordinary travel factors affecting everyone; they do not move trans risk.
blindSourceSummaries: A national alert desk documented more than 1,000 anti-LGBTQ incidents nationwide in 2025; the state/provinces with the most: this state/province (198) and four others (72, 66, 50 and 50).

Analysis of 2025 incident data: this state/province recorded the most incidents of any state/province (198), and law-enforcement data shows "a dramatic increase" in anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports during the same period as the state/province governor's platforming of anti-trans figures.

July 2026 analysis: this state/province falls in the "safest laws" band (score 4.1) with 1.9 recorded incidents — the piece argues even the most protective law floors do not eliminate recorded hostility.

The state/province governor signed the law in September 2022, making this state/province the first sanctuary state/province for transgender youth seeking care: young people from other state/provinces can access hormones and puberty blockers here, and the law shields families from child-abuse investigations or criminal prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care.

rewrites.blindSummary:
The region contains two of the six regions with the highest recorded counts of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence in the 2012-2025 region-by-region study maintained by the country's principal LGBT monitoring project.

Against that stands the strongest judicial response to transphobic violence recorded anywhere in the country: in January 2025 a first-instance court in this region's main university city recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the association that supports trans sex workers, and - for the first time - admitted the national trans-movement organisation as civil party.

For a visitor the combination is specific: the highest-frequency regions of the country's violence record are here, but so is a documented court that named transphobic motive and ordered reparation.
rewrites.blindTangential: The Pride event was targeted politically over a conflict (June 2025 wave) - a protest-visibility climate affecting LGBT events generally rather than a trans-specific legal mechanism.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: A specialized prison section and the male-prison placement policy concern resident detainees; they do not change a visitor's exposure beyond the national prison framework.
blindSourceSummaries: A news-agency report (24 Jan 2025): a first-instance court in the region's main university city recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the trans-movement association that helps sex workers, and for the first time admitted the national trans-movement organisation as civil party - the strongest judicial recognition of transphobic aggravation recorded in this country.

A region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the country's regions with the highest victim counts, six of them ranking at the top; this record's region contains two of the six highest-victim regions, alongside four others. Provides the per-region violence distribution used to score all the country's units.

On August 30, 2025 the region's largest city's municipal administration announced that the country's highest administrative court, seated there, had upheld the city's 2022 removal of posters by an anti-trans campaign attacking 'gender' ideology in schools, on the ground that the images — one showing a boy being given a red hairbow — were discriminatory and that public spaces may not be used for messages that 'generate alarmism, fear or serious disturbance', particularly concerning minors. The anti-trans campaign behind the posters had collected 105,000 online signatures. The ruling is a dated judicial outcome in the region's largest city confirming that anti-trans public messaging can be restricted there, an institutional datapoint for this region record, which otherwise centres on violence statistics and the transphobic-motive verdict in the region's main university city.

On March 5, 2026 the country's highest ordinary court confirmed the appeal-court acquittal of a trans woman over the April 27, 2021 death of a man in the region's main university city, finding the death was caused by cardiac arrhythmia from accidental compression during a scuffle that the man started, making the acquittal on the charge of homicide final. The case was a national anti-trans media flashpoint, and the definitive judicial outcome favoured the trans defendant. For this record it documents that the region's courts and the highest ordinary court decided a high-profile trans-related case on the facts, complementing the record's claim about judicial responses to transphobic violence.

rewrites.blindSummary:
This region hosts the country's first and second practical civic gender-recognition schemes - chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges, created by a 2022 council motion brought by the country's first elected transgender councillor - and an analogous practice at the municipality and the public libraries. For a gender-nonconforming visitor these determine whether a ticket window or municipal desk becomes an argument.

Against this, the 2012-2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence names this region's two leading regions among the country's six highest-victim regions.
rewrites.blindTangential: A constituent region's 2015 regional-council motion 'in support of the natural family' and against 'gender ideology', and that region's rejection of sexuality-education standards, are a durable political-climate signal against LGBT+ rights generally, with no visitor-facing enforcement mechanism.
blindSourceSummaries: A city in this region inaugurated the country's first gender registry, letting transgender people use their chosen name on civic and municipal documents - presented as a milestone for transgender rights in the country; the record ties it to a 2022 council motion by the country's first elected transgender councillor, with another city's parallel practice at the municipality and libraries.

A region-and-city aggression breakdown 2012-2025: source for this record's claim that the region's two constituent regions rank among the country's six highest-victim regions for anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence.

rewrites.blindSummary:
The principal international LGBT-rights federation's annual country review (February 2025) finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people, with incidents reported almost monthly - and includes in that finding a March 2025 scooter-mounted homophobic assault on a young man in this region's largest metropolitan periphery.

In October 2025 at a commuter railway station in the region's main metropolitan area an activist - president of a local LGBT association - was subjected to an escalating verbal homophobic attack ending in threats of stabbing by two young men. The station setting is one any visitor could occupy. The underlying local-newspaper report was bot-blocked at fetch time; it is retained as a sourced event on the strength of the recorded claim.
rewrites.blindTangential: Every incident documented for this region targeted gay men rather than trans people specifically; a visitor-facing pattern of public-space homophobia that trans-presenting travellers share without being separately named.
blindSourceSummaries: An international LGBT federation's annual country review (February 2025): finds a troubling increase in the number and geographic spread of bias-motivated violence against LGBTI people in 2024, incidents reported almost monthly, including the March 2025 scooter-mounted assault of a young man in this region's largest metropolitan periphery.

A local news outlet (13 Oct 2025): a 63-year-old man was arrested after stabbing threats against a young LGBTQIA+ activist; a grave homophobic episode in this region's main metropolitan area, giving this record its region-specific violence datapoint.

rewrites.blindSummary:
Three trans women murdered in less than a week in July 2024 (one disappeared and found dead days later; one killed while sex work); four transfeminicides recorded in July 2024 alone and five for the year in the national NGO yearbook — second only to the country's capital. Activists reported six trans women killed in a short period and accused three levels of government of rights omissions. This state/province's penal code contains no transfeminicide offence, and its 2019 hate-crime provision covers sexual orientation but not gender identity — meaning a visitor assaulted in this state/province faces a legal framework with no specific protective category. The state/province has an anti-conversion-practices law carrying 2-5 years, and the national observatory's verdict on such statutes is that transfeminicide 'advances in law but not in sentences.'

Legislative response has been refusal: an initiative filed by a trans collective was 'ignored and finally lapsed,' prompting a 50+-day protest encampment outside the elected local legislature still ongoing in January 2026 (activists report harassment and lack of basic facilities at the camp). A deputy in 2026 could only ask the elected local legislature to 'unfreeze' the bill. There is no investigative unit, no protocol, and no named offence to invoke. The gap between nominal coverage and protection is documented in the observatory review 'transfeminicide advances in law but not in sentences.'

Context for comparison: the country's capital pairs a similar lethality record with a dedicated transfeminicide investigation unit (Dec 2024), mandatory-response protocols and a gender police force (Aug 2025); another state/province was first in the country to typify the crime (March 2024). This state/province's explicit legislative refusal is the opposite signal.
rewrites.blindTangential: The July 2024 killings cluster and the lapsed bill are transfeminicide-specific, but the broader 2024 record (51 hate crimes nationally, 56.86% trans women) shows a general hostility climate toward LGBT+ people that a non-trans gender-nonconforming visitor could also meet.
rewrites.blindLocalsOnly: Conversion-practice criminalisation (2-5 years) on the books but unenforced, and the absence of an administrative gender-recognition procedure, are resident-facing gaps.
blindSourceSummaries: A news outlet (31 Jul 2024): three trans women killed in this state/province in under a week — one, aged 23, killed while doing sex work, and a 27 Jun motel victim still unidentified; the state/province justice ministry issued no case information. Nationally at least 36 trans women were transfemicided in 2024; at least four in this state/province that year.

The country's longest-running civil-society hate-crime observatory yearbook (since 1998, May 2025): records the country's capital as the state/province with the most LGBT+ killings in 2024 (17 homicides, 11 trans women) ahead of this state/province (5); notes the country has no official registry of bias-motivated violence, and documents under-counting where media accounts lack victim names and gender data.

A fact-check outlet (2024): this state/province recorded 7 attacks on LGBT people, 3 forced disappearances and 4 transfeminicides during the year, and transfeminicide is not typified in the state/province penal code. A labour diagnostic survey found 42.2% of the state/province's trans population unemployed and 35.1% discriminated against at work.

A news outlet (12 Jan 2026): a trans collective has held a protest camp of more than 50 days outside the elected local legislature pressing legislators to typify transfeminicide in the state/province penal code; their bill was ignored for a year and lapsed, forcing a fresh filing.
